You are the VARIANTS BUILDER for the Rust crate at C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh. Read DESIGN.md and src/router.rs (shared Router trait, Task, seeded Rng — do not change). Other agents concurrently own src/hebbian.rs, src/baselines.rs, src/mesh.rs, src/main.rs (core) and src/sim.rs, src/stats.rs, src/bin/experiment.rs (benchmark). Do NOT edit those. Toolchain: in every Bash call first run:
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:/c/Users/mariu/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Packages/BrechtSanders.WinLibs.POSIX.UCRT_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe/mingw64/bin:$PATH"

Implement three variants identified by a research pass (crate sources at C:\Users\mariu\.cargo\registry\src\index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f\):
1. `PgActorRouter` (implements Router): policy-gradient three-factor rule inspired by ferromorphic `reinforce::Actor` (ferromorphic-0.23.2/src/reinforce.rs:417-500). select: theta summed over task features (+task_type), softmax over CANDIDATES only, sampled with our Rng. update: delta = reward - baseline[f] (per-feature EMA baseline); chosen a: theta[f][a] += eta*delta*(1-pi_a); other candidates b: theta[f][b] -= eta*delta*pi_b. Store the last candidate set/probabilities from select for the update. Config struct with Default; serde.
2. `RStdpRouter` (implements Router): reward-modulated STDP with an eligibility trace that persists across tasks. Prefer calling oxicuda_snn::plasticity::r_stdp::r_stdp_step (oxicuda-snn-0.5.5/src/plasticity/r_stdp.rs:83; read it — note same-step pre/post yields zero STDP, so use a 3-step protocol per task: pre=features, then post=onehot(chosen agent), then reward=reward-baseline). Features hashed to n_pre rows, agents = n_post columns. Score = weight row sums; softmax+epsilon select. If the crate API doesn't fit/compile, implement the same R-STDP rule natively and say so.
3. `TrustEdges`: hatcher-style asymmetric edge learning (hatcher-neural-1.0.0/src/trust.rs, equations.rs:122,240): per pair trust T += lambda*succ - mu*fail with mu > lambda (defaults 0.10 / 0.25), edge w += phi*T*(1-w) - psi*cost for pairs that carried traffic, unused edges w -= psi*cost (clamp [0,1]). Expose `pub fn record_team(&mut self, team: &[usize], reward: f64)`, `pub fn edge(&self,a,b)->f64`, `pub fn top_partners(&self, a, k, candidates)->Vec<usize>`, plus `pub fn fragility(&self, threshold) -> (usize, usize)` returning (bridges, articulation_points) of the thresholded edge graph using petgraph (`cargo add petgraph` — 0.8 is already in Cargo.lock). Design it so the mesh can swap its co-activation rule for this (document the exact hook).
Unit tests for each (convergence to best agent on a stationary toy; adaptation after drift for PgActor; trust asymmetry; fragility on a hand-built graph). Run cargo test --lib variants until green. Do not git commit.

Final report (concise): API of each variant, which crate code was used vs reimplemented, test results, and exactly how the benchmark builder should instantiate each one.

handback.t:
All three variants are written in `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\src\variants.rs` and `cargo test --lib variants` passes: 8 passed, 0 failed, no warnings from this file.

The only other edits were adding `pub mod variants;` to `src/lib.rs` and running `cargo add petgraph@0.8` (it resolves to 0.8.3). Nothing else was touched and nothing was committed.

## 1. PgActorRouter — implements `Router`, name "pg-actor"
- **API:**
  - `PgActorRouter::new(n_agents, PgActorConfig::default())`
  - `scores(&Task) -> Vec<f64>`: logits for every agent.
  - `policy(&Task, &[usize]) -> Vec<f64>`
  - Derives Serialize/Deserialize.
- **Config defaults:** `eta 0.5`, `baseline_alpha 0.1`, `baseline_init 0.5`, `theta_clip 3.0`, `epsilon 0.05`, `decay 0.01`.
- **Behaviour:** each agent's logit is the sum of `theta[key][agent]` over the task's features plus `type:<task_type>`. Softmax runs over the candidates only, and the router samples with our `Rng`. `select` stores the candidates and probabilities for `update`.
- **Update:** per key, `delta = reward - baseline[key]`. The chosen agent gets `+eta*delta*(1-pi)`, every other candidate gets `-eta*delta*pi`, and the per-key EMA baseline then moves toward the reward.
- **Crate code:** reimplemented natively. `ferromorphic::reinforce::Actor` only handles separate numbered states, with no feature sums, and has its own Rng, so it doesn't fit.
- **Two additions beyond the spec:** `epsilon` exploration and `decay` (row decay per update). Without them the drift test failed: only the task type whose best agent didn't change was routed right (0.33). The softmax saturates, the old favourite's `(1-pi)` gradient goes to ~0, and the new best agent is never tried. Both are config fields, so they can be set to 0.

## 2. RStdpRouter — implements `Router`, name "r-stdp"
- **API:**
  - `RStdpRouter::new(n_agents, RStdpRouterConfig::default())`
  - `scores(&Task)`: sums of the weights on the task's active rows, per agent.
  - `weight(row, agent)`
  - `ensure_agents(n)`: grows the agent dimension (also done automatically).
  - Derives Serialize/Deserialize.
- **Config defaults:** `n_pre 64`, `a_plus = a_minus = 1.0`, `tau_plus = tau_minus = 2`, `tau_e 2`, `eta 1.0`, `w_init 0.5`, `temperature 0.1`, `epsilon 0.02`, `baseline_alpha 0.1`, `baseline_init 0.5`.
- **Crate code is used:** `oxicuda_snn::plasticity::r_stdp::r_stdp_step` is called directly, and its state is moved in and out with `mem::take`, so nothing is copied.
- **Three steps per task:**
  1. pre = hashed feature rows (FNV-1a), no post spikes.
  2. post = one-hot of the chosen agent.
  3. reward = reward minus the mean EMA baseline of the active rows.
- **Persistence:** the eligibility trace carries across tasks. The fast spike traces (x_pre/y_post) are reset at the start of each task, so the previous task's post spike can't cause spurious LTD.
- **Select:** epsilon-greedy plus softmax over candidates.

## 3. TrustEdges — co-activation rule, not a Router
- **API:**
  - `TrustEdges::new(n_agents, TrustEdgesConfig::default())`
  - `record_team(&[usize], reward)`
  - `edge(a, b) -> f64` and `trust(a, b) -> f64`
  - `top_partners(a, k, candidates) -> Vec<usize>`: sorted by weight descending, ties by index.
  - `fragility(threshold) -> (bridges, articulation_points)`, using petgraph `algo::bridges` and `algo::articulation_points`.
  - `graph(threshold)`, `ensure_agents(n)`, `set_edge(a, b, w)`
  - Derives Serialize/Deserialize.
- **Config defaults** (hatcher's defaults): `lambda 0.10`, `mu 0.25`, `phi 0.15`, `psi 0.05`, `cost 0.20`, `initial_trust 0.5`, `initial_weight 0.10`.
- **Update:** reward counts as fractional success (reward) and failure (1 - reward). Team pairs: trust `T = clamp(T + lambda*succ - mu*fail)`, then weight `w += phi*T*(1-w) - psi*cost`. Every other pair: `w -= psi*cost`. All values stay in [0,1].
- **Crate code:** the hatcher equations are reimplemented on plain Vecs.
- **Caveat for tuning:** trust only rises for pairs whose success rate is above mu/(lambda+mu) = 0.714. Unused edges lose 0.01 per call.

**Mesh hook** (also written in the module doc):
- **`NeuralMesh::feedback`:** replace the `team.len() >= 2` block (edge decay plus `edge_eta*(reward-baseline)`) with `trust_edges.record_team(team, reward)`.
- **`NeuralMesh::route_k`:** have `NeuralMesh::edge(a, b)` return `trust_edges.edge(a, b)`, or call `trust_edges.top_partners(leader, k-1, &rest)`.
- **`ensure_agents`:** forward it to `TrustEdges::ensure_agents`.
- Weights are in [0,1], not mesh's [-1,1].

## Tests (all pass)
- **PG actor:** converges on a stationary toy (best-agent share above 0.8 over the last 600 of 3000 tasks), and adapts after drift (above 0.7 over the last 600 of 4000 tasks). Selection stays within the candidate set, and state survives a JSON round-trip.
- **R-STDP:** converges (above 0.75). A reward above baseline strengthens the chosen agent and one below weakens it, and state survives a JSON round-trip.
- **TrustEdges:** trust is asymmetric (+0.10 vs -0.25, and alternating success/failure ends net negative). A reliable pair's edge grows above 0.5, an unused edge decays to 0, and a failing pair's edge drops to 0. On a hand-built graph, fragility gives (2, 2) at threshold 0.5 and (3, 3) at 0.1.

## How the benchmark builder should instantiate them
```rust
use neural_mesh::variants::*;
let pg   = PgActorRouter::new(n_agents, PgActorConfig::default());      // Router
let rs   = RStdpRouter::new(n_agents, RStdpRouterConfig::default());    // Router
let mesh_pg = NeuralMesh::new(n_agents, PgActorRouter::new(n_agents, PgActorConfig::default()), MeshConfig::default());
let mut te = TrustEdges::new(n_agents, TrustEdgesConfig::default());
// per team task: te.record_team(&team, reward); helpers via te.top_partners(leader, k-1, &candidates)
```
- Both routers derive Clone, so they work with mesh's `team_size = 1` equivalence check.
- PgActorRouter and RStdpRouter also accept candidate indices beyond `n_agents` and grow to fit.
- Defaults have not been tuned on seeds 1-8.
- TrustEdges can't be benchmarked as a mesh rule until `mesh.rs` (owned by the core agent) adds the hook above. Until then, use it as a separate structure next to the mesh.
